content: Small-minded people blame others. Average people blame themselves. The wise see all blame as foolishness.
author: Epictetus
story:
At its core, this reflection cuts through our everyday excuses. Holding onto anger is like clutching a glowing coal with the intent of throwing it at someone else—you are the one who gets burned. Retaliation only ties you tighter to the person who harmed you.

In Epictetus's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. Forgiveness and composure are not signs of weakness or giving someone a pass. They are acts of fierce self-preservation, cutting the emotional chain that allows another person's bad behavior to ruin your peace of mind.
reflectionPrompt: In what area of your life are you overthinking the ideal approach instead of taking the simple, honorable action?

practicalInsight: When someone triggers your temper today, take three slow breaths before responding. Do not give away your power for the sake of a quick comeback.
originalQuote: The wise man, when he does anything wrong, does not blame others, nor does he accuse himself, but he blames the thing which produced the wrong.
